article: Article 5.3.4 (SBIE tangible asset carve-out, permanent 5% rate)
fact_pattern: Eligible tangible assets average carrying value = 100 (units). Applicable carve-out rate = 5% (permanent rate under Art. 5.3.4; transitional rate would differ by fiscal-year start).
result: SBIE tangible-asset component = 5. This is a rule-knowledge illustration, not a reproduced published example figure.
weakest_point: No published Example 5.3.4 numeric output was retrievable in the search material; the 5% rate and 100 base are illustrative.

fact_pattern: FY beginning 2025. Payroll = 40, Tangible assets avg carrying value = 60. Adjusted Covered Taxes = 8, Net GloBE Income = 100. (ETR pre-calc 8%.)
computation: Payroll carve-out = 9.6% × 40 = 3.84; Tangible carve-out = 7.6% × 60 = 4.56; SBIE = 3.84 + 4.56 = 8.4; Excess Profit = 100 − 8.4 = 91.6; Top-up % = 15% − 8% = 7%; Top-up Tax = 7% × 91.6 = 6.412.
weakest_point: The fact pattern (40/60/100/8) appears in secondary summaries; the exact OECD example label and stated result were not directly retrieved from the OECD PDF in the search material.

article: Article 9.1.2 (transition rule – deferred tax asset from permanent-difference tax incentive excluded)
fact_pattern: Dec 2021: asset purchased for 100. Domestic CIT rate 25%. Immediate expensing of 100 plus additional 300 tax depreciation incentive in 2021. Domestic tax loss = 300, DTA established. As the DTA relating to the supplemental 300 reverses, question is whether it is included in Adjusted Covered Taxes.
computation: The 300 supplemental depreciation is a permanent difference for GloBE purposes (not part of GloBE income computation). Under Art. 9.1.2, DTAs generated after 30 Nov 2021 from such excluded items are not imported. Therefore, as that DTA reverses, the deferred tax expense is NOT included in Adjusted Covered Taxes.
result: The reversing deferred tax benefit (up to 25% × 300 = 75) is excluded from Adjusted Covered Taxes. The example in the Commentary states it is 'not included in Adjusted Covered Taxes under the application of this Article.'
weakest_point: Exact numeric deferred tax amount (75) is derived from 25% × 300; the published example's phrasing emphasizes the qualitative exclusion rather than stating a specific DTA euro figure.

fact_pattern: Jurisdiction H: CbCR revenue < 10, profit before tax < 1. (Transitional CbCR Safe Harbour de minimis test.)
computation: If 3-year avg GloBE revenue < EUR 10m AND 3-year avg Net GloBE Income < EUR 1m (or loss), the jurisdiction qualifies; Top-up Tax = 0.
result: Top-up tax deemed zero for the year.
weakest_point: Specific 3-year numeric sequences from a published Example 5.5.2 were not directly retrieved; the threshold logic is per Art. 5.5.1/5.5.2.

fact_pattern: Jurisdiction L, FY2024. Net GloBE Income = 100. Adjusted Covered Taxes = 10. Eligible payroll = 50, Eligible tangible assets avg = 200.
computation: ETR = 10/100 = 10%; Top-up % = 15% − 10% = 5%; FY2024 transitional rates: payroll 9.8%, tangible 7.8%; Payroll carve-out = 9.8% × 50 = 4.9; Tangible carve-out = 7.8% × 200 = 15.6; SBIE = 20.5; Excess Profit = 100 − 20.5 = 79.5; Top-up Tax = 5% × 79.5 = 3.975.
weakest_point: The 100/10/50/200 fact pattern is from secondary illustrative material; the precise OECD example number (e.g., 'Example 5.2.1-1') and its official stated result were not directly extracted from the OECD 2025 Examples PDF in the search material.
